analysis.title: 2027 Treasury supply & debt limit outlook
key_insights: CA CIB expects the US Treasury to keep coupon auction sizes unchanged in the near term and to raise them in H2 2027, mostly in the two- to seven-year sector, starting in August 2027.
Long-end coupon issuance is the main uncertainty. Treasury is still assessing investor demand, market functioning and cost to taxpayers under different financing strategies.
CA CIB expects TIPS auction sizes to stay broadly unchanged throughout 2027.
Gross coupon issuance is forecast to rise to about USD4.5trn in 2027 from USD4.4trn in 2026. Net marketable borrowing is forecast at roughly USD2.1trn in 2027.

Bill supply should fall in December on corporate and non-withheld tax receipts, then rise in January as seasonal spending increases. Net bill issuance is estimated at USD800-900bn in 2027, against c.USD721bn net issued in FY2026.

Bills are about USD7.4trn, or 23% of marketable debt, below historical peaks. That leaves room to rely more on bills and shorten weighted average maturity (WAM). Any signal of a modest WAM shortening would likely support longer-dated Treasuries by easing long-end supply pressure.

Bill demand is supported by money market funds, which hold nearly USD8trn in assets (c.USD6.6trn in government funds), and by New York Fed bill purchases from MBS reinvestments (c.USD14bn over the next four weeks).
The Fed announced on 13 November that it would not buy bills for reserve management purposes over the next four weeks. That policy has been in place since mid-August.
Treasury debt is projected to reach the USD41.1trn statutory limit in early 2027. Extraordinary measures worth a few hundred USDbn would then sustain operations for several months.
The debt limit X-date is expected in Q4 2027, when extraordinary measures and the TGA are exhausted and markets begin pricing default risk.

Ahead of the X-date, Treasury is expected to cut bill issuance and draw down the TGA, which raises bank reserves. Money market funds would shift from bills to repo, putting downward pressure on repo rates.
After Congress raises or suspends the limit, Treasury will rebuild the TGA through heavy bill issuance. That drains reserves and redirects money market fund flows back to bills.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Modest rise from USD4.4trn in 2026, driven by increases in two- to seven-year auction sizes from August 2027.
Higher than FY2026 given deficit size. The amount depends on debt-limit timing and resolution.
Treasury's own projection. CA CIB expects the TGA to fall sharply in Q2 and Q3 2027 as in prior debt limit episodes.
Treasury debt is projected to reach it, triggering extraordinary measures.
Cash and extraordinary measures run out, and default risk starts to be priced.

risk_factors: Debt limit negotiations may create significant volatility in the TGA and bill issuance.
Markets begin pricing default risk as the X-date approaches in Q4 2027.
Long-end issuance policy is uncertain and depends on demand, market functioning and taxpayer cost.
The Fed's pause in reserve management bill purchases removes one source of bill demand. MBS reinvestment purchases continue.
vol_and_positioning: Money market funds hold nearly USD8trn in assets, c.USD6.6trn of it in government funds, and are significant bill buyers.
Falling bill supply ahead of the X-date would push money market funds into repo and put downward pressure on repo rates.
